# Knowledge Cache

Date-tagged, reusable facts learned from web research in this project. Persistent across sessions; read this index first before calling `tavily_*`, `firecrawl_*`, or `context7_*` to avoid re-fetching the same answer.

## Convention

- **Path:** `.agents/docs/cache/<topic>/YYYY-MM-DD-<short-slug>.md` — one topic per file, ISO date prefix sorts chronologically.
- **Index:** this file lists every entry with relative link, topic, source URL, capture date, and a freshness note.
- **Scope:** only persistent, reusable, volatile facts belong here. One-off answers, scratchpads, and transient work go in `.tmp/`.
- **Re-verify:** CLI tool / framework APIs are volatile — re-verify if the entry is more than 6 months old, or if the domain has had a major release.

Sources: MiniMax Responses/Chat/Anthropic API refs, MiniMax function-call guide, HF/GitHub model cards, live OpenRouter probes.

- [2026-09-09 — verifier disagreement resolution (shiki + reki)](kilo-subagents/2026-09-09-verifier-disagreement-resolution.md) — two-stage tie-break algorithm: stage 1 main-agent-resolves (≤ 3 tool calls, ≤ 30s reasoning) for phrasing-artefact and evidence-asymmetry disagreements (~70-85% of cases, $0); stage 2 targeted 4-season fan-out with aki+fuyu (interpretive roles only) for interpretation-asymmetry (~15-30%, ~$0.025–0.035 + 80-120s). Skip stage 1 when security-critical, recurring disagreement type, or both verifier reasonings < 100 tokens. Persistent disagreement (stage 2 also disagrees) → report to user with flag, not silent pick. Includes the YAML reconciliation block for reki.md and the disagreement_diagnosis checklist.

- [2026-09-09 — does telling a subagent another subagent's (or its own) model name in the system prompt improve output?](kilo-subagents/2026-09-09-agent-prompt-peer-identity-evidence.md) — evidence synthesis for the reki/shiki/fleet bodies. **Verdict: harmful on balance for the disagreement-detection signal.** Choi et al. 2026 (ACL 2026 Main) empirically shows identity disclosure in MAD prompts causes sycophancy/self-bias; Lu et al. 2025-12 shows cross-family verifier pairs have lower FPR than intra-family/self (architecture does the work, prompt text doesn't need to narrate). Reki's literal model-name disclosure at `reki.md:155-158` partially cancels the anti-anchoring stance — keep the stance, drop the names. Sources: arXiv 2510.07517, 2604.22971, 2512.02304, 2507.11662, 2605.25133, 2604.02770, 2510.05174, 2505.16979, 2410.13787, 2501.11120, 2507.17257.

Both verdicts converged but reki's caveat-discovery proves the cross-family decorrelation is doing its job. 4 artefacts produced (shiki/reki round 1, shiki/reki round 2).

### kilo-modes

Custom primary-agent modes for Kilo CLI and the VS Code extension. Distinct from subagents: modes are picked from `/agents` and run as the main loop.

- [2026-08-25 — assist-only mode: principal-engineer reviewer](kilo-modes/2026-08-25-assist-only-mode.md) — global mode at `~/.config/kilo/mode/assist-only.md` (deployed via chezmoi). Same tool surface as `code`; `read` is filtered against the project's sensitive-file list (AGENTS.md §"Sensitive File Handling") and `edit` is globbed to `.tmp/scratch/assist-only/` (demo sandbox) + the mode file + `docs/assist-only/` + `.agents/docs/cache/`. Production code is the user's job; demonstrative code is allowed in the sandbox with a `REFERENCE — not for merge` marker. `bash` allowed for smoke tests (soft-cap persona guardrails). Anti-assumption protocol forces the user to ground every claim. Layered over the github/spec-kit loop (constitution → specify → clarify → plan → tasks → analyze → checklist → converge). Companion skill at `~/.config/kilo/skills/spec-kit/SKILL.md`. Sources: kilocode source, kilo-config skill, kilo-subagents cache, spec-kit v1.0.0.
